HairDeck: Animation-Ready Stylized Hair Cards from a Single Image 

 Yuze He 1,   Yixiang Wei 1,   Wang Zhao 1   Chuhao Chen 2   Yanning Zhou 3,†   Yong-Jin Liu 1,† 
 1 Tsinghua University   2 Carnegie Mellon University   3 The Chinese University of Hong Kong 
 Equal contribution.   † Corresponding authors. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 English · 简体中文 · 日本語 

 🔥 Updates

- [2026.11.05] 🎨 Colored hair cards: a color model predicts the colors along every card, from two-tone hair to accessories, and the GLB and VRM exports carry them. Try it in the online demo.
- [2026.11.03] 🍎 Apple silicon support: HairDeck runs on MPS (same pipeline, no CUDA or Triton). Get started.
- [2026.11.02] 🎉 Windows support is here! Run HairDeck with local Gradio, VRM export and automatic model offload. Get started.
- [2026.10.30] 🎉 HairDeck is released! Code, model weights and the online demo are available.

 

 Video

 

 Overview

 HairDeck generates stylized hair cards and the spring-bone chains that animate them from a single image. 
Each hair card is represented by one token, and a set diffusion transformer generates the cards jointly.
The generated hairstyle can be exported as a GLB mesh or attached to an avatar and exported as VRM.

- Hair cards as a set. A card VAE encodes each card, and conditional set diffusion generates the hairstyle as a whole.
- Geometry with UVs. The output preserves individual hair cards and provides per-card UV coordinates.
- Colors from the image. A color model predicts the colors along every card, including two-tone hair and accessories.
- Spring-bone animation. A chain diffusion model generates the bones that drive the cards, with skinning and VRM export.

 
 
 

 Getting started

 🛠️ Installation

HairDeck runs on Linux and native Windows with an NVIDIA CUDA GPU, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.8 and CUDA 12.8. Apple
silicon Macs run it on MPS (see macOS below).

 Windows: Follow Windows setup to install the environment and launch Gradio.

 macOS (Apple silicon): Follow macOS setup: the same pipeline runs on Apple MPS, without CUDA or Triton.

 AMD ROCm (Linux): See ROCm setup for the tested Radeon 8060S / Strix Halo container, including HIP-enabled torchvision and headless rendering.

 --n accepts 1–4 variations; --seed sets the first seed. Use --no-chains to generate cards only, and --no-colors for one hair color.

 📊 Test-set evaluation

On Linux, download the evaluation assets, then run the point-cloud and chain tests. Each test samples seeds 0, 1 and 2,
prints the corresponding paper metrics, and saves per-sample results and their means in eval.json .

 

Evaluation paths such as results/pointcloud follow the workspace layout under HAIRDECK ROOT and its path overrides.

 🧩 Community

- ComfyUI-HairDeck by visualbruno: ComfyUI nodes for HairDeck, with GLB, rigged GLB and VRM export and the color model.

 

 📝 Citation

 

 Acknowledgments

HairDeck uses CHARM, Dora-VAE, DINOv3, SAM 3, BiRefNet, and the VRM Add-on for Blender. We thank their authors for making these resources available.

install.html:
🛠️ Installation · 🤗 Model weights · 🚀 Quick start · 🖼️ Local demo · 📦 Outputs · 📊 Evaluation · 🏋️ Training · 📝 Citation

🛠️ Installation

HairDeck runs on Linux and native Windows with an NVIDIA CUDA GPU, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.8 and CUDA 12.8. Apple silicon Macs run it on MPS (see macOS below).

Windows: Follow Windows setup to install the environment and launch Gradio.

macOS (Apple silicon): Follow macOS setup: the same pipeline runs on Apple MPS, without CUDA or Triton.

AMD ROCm (Linux): See ROCm setup for the tested Radeon 8060S / Strix Halo container, including HIP-enabled torchvision and headless rendering.

Linux: Install the dependencies below and make ffmpeg available on your PATH.

git clone https://github.com/hyz317/HairDeck.git
cd HairDeck

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pip install --no-deps pyrender==0.1.45  # without its old PyOpenGL pin

Run the commands below from the repository root, in the same Python environment.

🤗 Model weights

Our checkpoints and supporting assets are hosted at hyz317/HairDeck. SAM 3 and DINOv3 are gated: first accept their licences on facebook/sam3 and facebook/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m, then log in:

hf auth login
export HAIRDECK_ROOT=/path/to/workspace  # checkpoints, data, third-party weights and outputs
python scripts/setup/download_weights.py

Chinese users can refer to the Chinese README for download instructions.

The downloader sets up the HairDeck checkpoints, preprocessing and image-encoder weights, supporting data, and Blender 4.2 LTS with the VRM Add-on. The downloader selects the Blender build for your operating system. To use an existing Blender 4.2 LTS installation with the VRM Add-on enabled, set HAIRDECK_BLENDER to its command.

The default workspace layout is:

$HAIRDECK_ROOT/
├── ckpt/                       # HairDeck checkpoints and latent statistics
├── data/                       # Normalization statistics, avatar and demo examples
└── third_party/
    ├── weights/
    │   ├── dinov3/             # facebook/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m
    │   ├── sam3/               # facebook/sam3
    │   └── birefnet_matting/    # ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet-matting
    ├── dinov3_src/             # DINOv3 source
    ├── sam3_src/               # SAM 3 source
    └── blender/                # Blender and the VRM Add-on

Individual locations can be configured through environment variables or a JSON file; see configs/paths.example.json and hairdeck/paths.py.

🚀 Quick start

Generate four variations from a character image, then export variation 0 as a VRM avatar and a head-turn video:

python scripts/image_to_hair.py character.png --out results/my_character --n 4
python -m hairdeck.vrm.export results/my_character/character 0

Results are written to OUT/<image name>/, here results/my_character/character/. --n accepts 1–4 variations; --seed sets the first seed. Use --no-chains to generate cards only, and --no-colors for one hair color. For custom models, pass --ckpt and a matching --chain_ckpt trained with the same card VAE. Set HAIRDECK_FAST=1 to sample with the fast sampler (2-3x faster sampling at small batch sizes, measured on NVIDIA and AMD; on by default with ROCm).

🖼️ Local demo
python -m pip install -r requirements-demo.txt
python demo/app.py --port 7860

Open http://127.0.0.1:7860 to generate hair, inspect variations, and export a VRM or animation preview. You can also try the hosted demo.
